prompt:
One image: a sprite sheet of 10 different cars for a 2D top-down city game, every car seen straight down from above (orthographic), on a fully transparent background.

The attached image shows finished cars from the same game. Match its art style exactly — outline weight, shading, highlights, level of detail, pixel size — but not its cars or their colours.

Layout: a 4×3 grid, the cars in the order listed below, left to right and top to bottom. Every car lies horizontally with its nose pointing right, centred in its place in the grid, with clear empty space between neighbours and round the picture's edge. All cars are drawn on one shared scale: a car listed as 4.5 m long is half as long again as one listed as 3 m.

Every car:
- Its length and width as listed, and exactly the proportion given: how many times longer than wide it is. Seen from above its body is a rounded rectangle with straight flanks.
- Each is a believable everyday car of a real kind, as seen in an Eastern European city today.
- No tyres or wheels visible: the game draws them under the body. Roof on: no convertible, no open top, no seats or people. Mirror-symmetric about its long centre line. Two small side mirrors just ahead of the windscreen.
- Every lamp a real car has, all switched off — unlit glass with one small pale glint, no glow, no light cast: a headlamp at each front corner with an amber indicator at its outer end; at each rear corner a rear lamp cluster holding a red tail and brake lamp, an amber indicator and a white reversing lamp. Draw them in the shapes this kind of car has.
- Each lamp's glass is outlined by a thin dark frame, so every lens stands clearly apart from the paint round it. One lamp unit at each corner, never a light bar across the whole nose or tail.
- Condition shows in the paint only — faded colour, small rust spots, a panel a slightly different shade. The body is whole: no dents big enough to change the outline, no holes, nothing missing.
- Bonnet, roof and boot read as separate panels, divided by the windscreen and the rear window.
- No text, logos, brand badges, licence plates, numbers or watermark anywhere.
- Outside the cars the picture is fully transparent: no background colour, no ground, no shadow, nothing half-transparent.
